phases.title: Foundation
phases.outcome: Build a reliable 6.0 foundation and begin reaching 6.5 through evidence.

phases.title: Accuracy
phases.outcome: Make band 6 performance stable and reduce recurring errors.

phases.title: Build Band 6.5
phases.outcome: Produce controlled band 6.5 work across all four skills.

phases.title: Exam Performance
phases.outcome: Convert ability into repeatable performance under full test conditions.

phases.title: Peak & Test
phases.outcome: Meet the target in consecutive mocks and arrive at the test rested.

prelaunch.title: Collect recent Writing class recordings
prelaunch.objective: Prepare four to six recent Task 1 and Task 2 recordings for ChatGPT.
steps: List the recordings from newest to oldest.
Label each recording Task 1 or Task 2.
Choose the four to six lessons most relevant to your current method.
prelaunch.output: A short list of selected recordings with dates and lesson types.
doneWhen: Every selected recording has a date.
Every selected recording is labelled Task 1 or Task 2.

prelaunch.title: Build the first course knowledge notes
prelaunch.objective: Let ChatGPT extract reusable knowledge from recent lessons before August.
steps: Send one selected recording or transcript to ChatGPT.
Ask ChatGPT to extract the lesson method, examples, teacher feedback and homework.
Check the summary and import the structured course session into Joy.
prelaunch.output: At least one reviewed Course Session in Joy.
doneWhen: The lesson summary is saved.
The method and next practice are recorded separately.

prelaunch.title: Prepare the August baseline
prelaunch.objective: Confirm that the official four-skill baseline links and test setup are ready before 1 August.
steps: Open each attached official IELTS source only far enough to confirm that it loads.
Do not preview the questions, prompts, recordings or answers.
Prepare a timer, microphone, headphones and a quiet study space.
Use the direct links attached to each baseline task on 1–2 August.
prelaunch.output: All official baseline links load and the test setup is ready for 1–2 August.
doneWhen: All four official source links are available in the baseline tasks.
The timer, audio and Speaking recording setup work.
No test content or answers have been previewed.
prelaunch.material: Official IELTS Academic sample-test hub and computer practice experience.

baseline.objective: Measure current ability before personalising the first study rhythm.

tasks.title: Full Listening baseline
tasks.objective: Measure Listening performance and identify the causes of lost marks.
steps: Open the attached official Listening test only when you are ready to begin.
Set a 30-minute timer because the official practice interface is not timed.
Complete all 40 questions without pausing or replaying the recordings.
Check every answer after finishing the full test.
Classify each mistake as comprehension, spelling, distraction or prediction.
tasks.output: Answer score, source and a categorised mistake list.
doneWhen: All questions are completed under test conditions.
Every wrong answer has a reason.
tasks.material: Official IELTS Academic computer practice: full Listening test, 4 parts and 40 questions.

tasks.title: Full Academic Reading baseline
tasks.objective: Measure Reading accuracy, timing and weak question types.
steps: Open the attached official Academic Reading test only when you are ready to begin.
Set a strict 60-minute timer because the official practice interface is not timed.
Complete all three passages and 40 questions without a dictionary.
Check the answers and locate evidence for every wrong or guessed answer.
Record passage timing, time pressure and weak question types.
tasks.output: Answer score, passage timing and an evidence-based error list.
doneWhen: The full test is completed in 60 minutes.
Every wrong or guessed answer is reviewed.
tasks.material: Official IELTS Academic computer practice: full Academic Reading test, 3 passages and 40 questions.

tasks.title: Full Writing baseline
tasks.objective: Measure unaided Task 1 and Task 2 performance.
steps: Open the attached official Writing test only when you are ready to begin.
Write Task 1 in 20 minutes and Task 2 in 40 minutes.
Do not use ChatGPT, a dictionary, grammar tools or sample answers while writing.
After the 60-minute test, send both unchanged responses to ChatGPT for criterion-based feedback.
Save the estimated scores, evidence and recurring errors.
tasks.output: Two timed responses and one structured assessment.
doneWhen: Both responses were written without help.
Feedback covers all four Writing criteria.
tasks.material: Official IELTS Academic computer practice: one Task 1 prompt and one Task 2 prompt.

tasks.title: Full Speaking baseline
tasks.objective: Measure fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation across all three parts.
steps: Open the attached official Speaking sample only when you are ready to begin.
Start with ChatGPT and ask it to act as the examiner using the official prompts without showing future questions.
Complete and record Parts 1, 2 and 3 in one continuous mock.
Listen once and note pauses, repetition and unclear answers.
Send the recording or transcript to ChatGPT for structured feedback.
tasks.output: One full recording, transcript notes and assessment.
doneWhen: All three Speaking parts are completed.
The main fluency and language problems are recorded.
tasks.material: Official IELTS Speaking sample tasks: Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3 prompts in one PDF.

weeks.title: Foundation & Error Awareness
weeks.outcome: Explain the baseline errors and use a clear structure before adding speed.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 1
rhythms.objective: Repair the weakest Listening and Reading patterns and build clear Speaking Part 1 answers.

tasks.title: Repair the two weakest Listening question types
tasks.objective: Understand why baseline answers were lost and practise the same patterns deliberately.
steps: Give ChatGPT your baseline error categories.
Complete two short drills selected from the weakest question types.
Use the transcript to identify the exact missed language.
Repeat the difficult audio once after correction.
tasks.output: Two corrected drills and a short list of listening signals.
doneWhen: Every incorrect answer has transcript evidence.
At least one repeated error has a prevention rule.

tasks.title: Repair the two weakest Reading question types
tasks.objective: Replace guessing with a repeatable evidence-finding process.
steps: Give ChatGPT the weakest Reading question types.
Complete one focused passage without a strict time limit.
Underline evidence for every answer.
Explain why each distractor is wrong.
tasks.output: One annotated passage and a question-type strategy.
doneWhen: Every answer has evidence.
The strategy is recorded in your own words.

tasks.title: Build complete Speaking Part 1 answers
tasks.objective: Answer familiar questions naturally without stopping after one sentence.
steps: Ask ChatGPT for ten Part 1 questions matched to your learner profile.
Answer and record all ten.
Expand weak answers with a reason or example.
Record the five weakest answers again.
tasks.output: Ten answers and five improved recordings.
doneWhen: Each answer directly answers the question.
Weak answers have been recorded a second time.

tasks.title: Create the first recurring-error map
tasks.objective: Turn baseline findings into priorities for the next rhythm.
steps: Select no more than five recurring errors.
Record the cause and one prevention action for each.
Share the updated Joy context with ChatGPT.
doneWhen: Every error has a cause and next action.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 2
rhythms.objective: Capture the Task 1 course method and apply it to one controlled response.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Wednesday
tasks.objective: Learn the scheduled Task 1 content from the external course.
steps: Attend the class.
Save the lesson recording.
Record the topic, homework and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class is attended.
The recording or lesson source is saved.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Thursday
tasks.objective: Continue the scheduled Task 1 content from the external course.
steps: Attend the class.
Save the lesson recording.
Record new instructions and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class is attended.
The recording or lesson source is saved.

tasks.title: Process both Task 1 lesson recordings
tasks.objective: Turn the two class recordings into reusable course knowledge.
steps: Send the recordings or transcripts to ChatGPT.
Extract method, examples, teacher feedback and homework.
Import the two Course Sessions into Joy.
doneWhen: Both sessions have a summary and next practice.

tasks.title: Apply the Task 1 lesson
tasks.objective: Use the course method in a new Task 1 plan, overview and selected paragraph.
steps: Ask ChatGPT for a prompt that matches the lesson topic.
Identify key features and plan the response.
Write the overview and one body paragraph.
Check whether the course method was applied correctly.
tasks.output: One Task 1 plan, overview and body paragraph.
doneWhen: Key features are selected.
The response uses the method from class.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 3
rhythms.objective: Capture the Task 2 method, practise paragraph development and close the first week.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 2 class · Friday
tasks.objective: Learn the scheduled Task 2 content from the external course.
steps: Attend the class.
Save the lesson recording.
Record homework and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class is attended.
The recording or lesson source is saved.

tasks.title: Build one complete Task 2 body paragraph
tasks.objective: Develop one main idea with explanation and a relevant example.
steps: Process the Friday lesson with ChatGPT.
Analyse one paragraph using the class method.
Brainstorm one main idea for a new prompt.
Write, receive feedback and rewrite the paragraph.
tasks.output: One original paragraph, feedback and rewrite.
doneWhen: The paragraph directly answers the prompt.
The explanation and example support the same main idea.

tasks.title: Listening and Speaking maintenance
tasks.objective: Keep receptive and spoken English active during the Writing-heavy rhythm.
steps: Complete one short Listening section selected from the baseline weakness.
Record two Speaking Part 2 attempts.
Correct the main problem in each activity.
tasks.output: One corrected Listening section and two Speaking recordings.
doneWhen: Listening errors are reviewed.
The second Speaking attempt is clearer than the first.

tasks.title: Week 1 review
tasks.objective: Give ChatGPT enough evidence to prepare Week 2.
steps: Record the strongest improvement.
Record the most important recurring error.
Choose one priority for next week.
doneWhen: The review contains evidence, not only feelings.

weeks.title: Controlled Production
weeks.outcome: Complete full responses with support and begin using official time limits.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 1
rhythms.objective: Produce timed Listening and Reading work and sustain longer Speaking answers.

tasks.title: Timed Listening Sections 3–4
tasks.objective: Follow longer academic discussions and monologues without replaying.
steps: Complete Sections 3–4 once under test conditions.
Check answers with the transcript.
Replay only the sentences that caused errors.
Record useful signals and distractors.
doneWhen: Every wrong answer has an audio or transcript explanation.

tasks.title: Two timed Reading passages
tasks.objective: Balance accuracy with a realistic passage time.
steps: Complete two passages using the time target agreed with ChatGPT.
Mark every guessed answer.
Find evidence for wrong and guessed answers.
Repeat the weakest question type.
tasks.output: Two scores, timing data and one focused correction drill.
doneWhen: Both passage times are recorded.
Guessed answers are reviewed even when correct.

tasks.title: Speaking Part 2 and Part 3 control
tasks.objective: Speak for close to two minutes and extend abstract answers.
steps: Prepare and record two Part 2 topics.
Answer six related Part 3 questions.
Ask ChatGPT to identify fluency and development problems.
Repeat the weakest Part 2 and three Part 3 answers.
tasks.output: Two Part 2 recordings and six Part 3 answers.
doneWhen: At least one Part 2 response approaches two minutes.
Part 3 answers include explanation or example.

tasks.title: Update language and error priorities
tasks.objective: Keep only errors that still affect performance.
steps: Update recurring errors.
Archive errors that no longer appear.
Share the context before Rhythm 2.
doneWhen: The active error list contains no more than five priorities.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 2
rhythms.objective: Use the external Task 1 lessons in one complete timed response.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Wednesday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 1 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and homework.
Record teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Thursday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 1 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and homework.
Record teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Process the Task 1 course knowledge
tasks.objective: Save only the reusable knowledge from both lessons.
steps: Process both records with ChatGPT.
Import lesson summaries and next practice into Course.
doneWhen: Both sessions are reviewed.

tasks.title: Write and revise one timed Task 1
tasks.objective: Complete Task 1 in 20 minutes and improve it using feedback.
steps: Ask ChatGPT for a prompt matching the class topic.
Write the response in 20 minutes.
Check it against the four Writing criteria.
Rewrite the weakest sections.
doneWhen: The first response was completed in 20 minutes.
The rewrite fixes the identified priority.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 3
rhythms.objective: Complete a timed Task 2 and apply feedback before the weekly review.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 2 class · Friday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 2 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and homework.
Record teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Write and revise one timed Task 2
tasks.objective: Complete Task 2 in 40 minutes and strengthen the weakest criterion.
steps: Process the Friday lesson with ChatGPT.
Write a matched Task 2 prompt in 40 minutes.
Receive criterion-based feedback.
Rewrite the introduction and weakest body paragraph.
doneWhen: The first response was completed in 40 minutes.
The rewrite addresses evidence from the assessment.

tasks.title: Speaking Part 2–3 application
tasks.objective: Use clearer development in both long turn and discussion answers.
steps: Complete one Part 2 topic.
Answer four related Part 3 questions.
Repeat answers after ChatGPT feedback.
tasks.output: One long turn and four discussion answers.
doneWhen: The repeated answers show a specific improvement.

tasks.title: Week 2 review
tasks.objective: Decide what must change before timed full tests.
steps: Record one measurable gain.
Record the most persistent problem.
Choose the Week 3 priority.
doneWhen: The priority is supported by task evidence.

weeks.title: Timed Control
weeks.outcome: Maintain quality across full timed tests and identify errors that survive instruction.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 1
rhythms.objective: Complete full Listening, Reading and Speaking checks under realistic conditions.

tasks.title: Full timed Listening check
tasks.objective: Test whether correction work transfers to a new full paper.
steps: Complete one new full Listening test.
Check every wrong or uncertain answer.
Compare error categories with baseline.
doneWhen: The test is completed without pausing.
Recurring errors are updated.

tasks.title: Full timed Academic Reading check
tasks.objective: Test accuracy and passage timing across a full paper.
steps: Complete one new full Reading test in 60 minutes.
Review wrong and guessed answers.
Compare question-type performance with baseline.
tasks.output: Full score, passage timing and comparison.
doneWhen: All passages are attempted.
Timing and errors are recorded.

tasks.title: Mid-month Speaking mock
tasks.objective: Check fluency and answer development across all three parts.
steps: Record a complete mock.
Ask ChatGPT for evidence-based feedback.
Repeat the weakest Part 2 or Part 3 response.
tasks.output: Full recording, assessment and one repeated response.
doneWhen: All three parts are completed.
Feedback is saved to Progress.

tasks.title: Save the mid-month checkpoint
tasks.objective: Compare current evidence with the baseline before planning the remaining rhythms.
steps: Save current skill estimates.
Record confidence and evidence for each estimate.
Share the checkpoint context with ChatGPT.
doneWhen: All four skill fields have evidence or are marked pending.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 2
rhythms.objective: Use Task 1 course knowledge accurately under the official time limit.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Wednesday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 1 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Thursday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 1 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Timed Task 1 with criterion review
tasks.objective: Produce and improve a full Task 1 using current course knowledge.
steps: Process the two lesson records with ChatGPT.
Write one matched Task 1 in 20 minutes.
Evaluate all four criteria.
Rewrite the response after feedback.
tasks.output: Two Course Sessions, timed response and rewrite.
doneWhen: Course knowledge is saved.
The rewrite fixes the weakest criterion.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 3
rhythms.objective: Produce Task 2 under time and attack the most persistent cross-skill errors.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 2 class · Friday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 2 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Timed Task 2 and targeted rewrite
tasks.objective: Maintain a clear position and develop ideas under time pressure.
steps: Process the Friday lesson with ChatGPT.
Write one matched Task 2 in 40 minutes.
Receive feedback and rewrite the weakest section.
tasks.output: Course Session, timed essay and rewrite.
doneWhen: The position is clear throughout.
The rewrite addresses the feedback.

tasks.title: Focused Speaking Part 3 drill
tasks.objective: Develop abstract answers with clear reasoning.
steps: Answer six Part 3 questions selected from the current weakness.
Receive feedback after each group of three.
Repeat the three weakest answers.
tasks.output: Six answers and three improved repeats.
doneWhen: Every repeated answer has a clear reason or example.

tasks.title: Drill the most persistent Listening or Reading error
tasks.objective: Prevent one recurring receptive-skill error from carrying into Week 4.
steps: Let ChatGPT select the highest-frequency error.
Complete a short targeted drill.
Record whether the prevention rule worked.
doneWhen: The result is added to the recurring-error record.

tasks.title: Week 3 review
tasks.objective: Select no more than three priorities for the final week.
steps: Compare current performance with baseline.
Choose the three highest-impact priorities.
doneWhen: Every priority is supported by recent evidence.

weeks.title: Stability & Assessment
weeks.outcome: Verify progress, stabilise the highest-impact gains and provide evidence for September.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 1
rhythms.objective: Complete final Listening, Reading and Speaking checks and compare them with baseline.

tasks.title: Final August Listening check
tasks.objective: Measure accuracy and recurring errors on a new full test.
steps: Complete a new full Listening test.
Review errors and compare them with baseline.
doneWhen: The test and correction are complete.

tasks.title: Final August Academic Reading check
tasks.objective: Measure full-test accuracy and timing against baseline.
steps: Complete a new full Reading test in 60 minutes.
Review wrong and guessed answers.
Compare passage timing with baseline.
doneWhen: All passages and corrections are complete.

tasks.title: Final August Speaking mock
tasks.objective: Measure fluency and answer development across all three parts.
steps: Record one full mock.
Receive evidence-based feedback.
Repeat the weakest response.
tasks.output: Final recording, assessment and repeated response.
doneWhen: The assessment is saved to Progress.

tasks.title: Prepare final Writing priorities
tasks.objective: Use the latest evidence to choose the final Writing focus.
steps: Review current Writing errors and course coverage.
Select one Task 1 and one Task 2 priority.
Share them with ChatGPT.
doneWhen: Both priorities are evidence-based.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 2
rhythms.objective: Complete the final Task 1 check and consolidate the month's course knowledge.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Wednesday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 1 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 1 class · Thursday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 1 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Final timed Task 1 and course audit
tasks.objective: Measure Task 1 performance and consolidate reusable course knowledge.
steps: Process both class records.
Write a matched Task 1 in 20 minutes.
Receive feedback and rewrite the response.
Mark course topics as learned, applied or still uncertain.
tasks.output: Two Course Sessions, final Task 1 and coverage audit.
doneWhen: The response is assessed.
Course coverage statuses are updated.

rhythms.label: Rhythm 3
rhythms.objective: Complete the final Writing check and close August with a structured review.

tasks.title: Attend external Task 2 class · Friday
tasks.objective: Learn and record the scheduled Task 2 lesson.
steps: Attend class.
Save the recording and teacher feedback.
doneWhen: The class source is saved.

tasks.title: Final full Writing check
tasks.objective: Measure Task 1 and Task 2 together under official time limits.
steps: Process the Friday course record.
Write Task 1 in 20 minutes and Task 2 in 40 minutes.
Receive criterion-based feedback.
Rewrite the sections that most reduce the estimated band.
tasks.output: Course Session, full Writing responses, assessment and rewrite.
doneWhen: Both tasks were completed in 60 minutes.
The assessment is saved to Progress.

tasks.title: Final weakest-skill drill
tasks.objective: Finish the month by practising the highest-impact unresolved weakness.
steps: Let ChatGPT choose one short drill from the latest evidence.
Complete and review it immediately.
doneWhen: The result is saved with the related error.

tasks.title: August monthly review
tasks.objective: Prepare the evidence ChatGPT needs to design September.
steps: Record the strongest measurable gain.
Record the most persistent problem.
Confirm the latest four-skill estimates.
Share the full Joy context with ChatGPT.
doneWhen: The review compares baseline and final evidence.
